svg.title: Inside the research agent
svg.desc: One LangGraph node containing planning, sequential sub-question search, evidence deduplication, up to two sufficiency checks and follow-up searches, and synthesis. A separate panel expands the reused search, rerank and grade helper. State returns to the graph before generation and verification.

text.tspan: Plan the work → collect evidence → organize findings → hand back to the graph
ENTRY · router chose intent=retrieval and complexity=research_required
State already contains the standalone question, allowed document types, access scope and company/year filters.
Example: “Compare Microsoft’s revenue in FY2016 and FY2023.”
Local variables and helper calls below; only the final return updates graph state.
Ask for 2–5 questions; code keeps at most 5.
Run the shared helper shown on the right →
Merge into chunks_by_id; keep each identity once.
Returns decision, missing quantity, follow-up, reason
Run the same helper with follow_up_question.
Add new unique chunks; retain earlier evidence.
An empty result adds nothing; it erases nothing.
Original question + plan + ALL full unique chunks
Organize values, units, sources, gaps and arithmetic.
Markdown findings: agent_synthesis, not the answer.
EXPANDED HELPER · called for every search
Keep access rules and company/year filters.
Voyage dense vector + local BM25 → Qdrant
Same mandatory filters; up to 50 candidates.
Return only accepted chunks to the caller.
Initial sub-questions run sequentially, not in parallel.
Both initial and follow-up searches reuse this same helper.
Useful enough to proceed; partial evidence is allowed.
It is not proof that every required quantity was found.
The second round may run one last follow-up search.
There is NO sufficiency check after that final search.
Only 400 characters/chunk go to this checker;
the synthesizer receives the full chunk text.
No final global “keep only 8” step in research.
Sub-questions change wording, not metadata filters.
No graph query-rewriter loop inside the helper.
Helpers are not separately checkpointed graph nodes.
it excludes embeddings, grades and SDK retries.
MAX_LLM_TURNS=5 is unused, not a total-call cap.
Detected provider limits abort to API error handling.
Other helper fallbacks are explained in the guide.
BACK IN LANGGRAPH · builder.py selects the next node
Check the draft against raw evidence, not synthesis alone.
Then follow the existing retry, approval and formatting routes.
Research findings are not directly released to the user.
Solid arrows show execution order. Dashed helper-call arrow expands ordinary Python work; it is not another graph edge.
Model names reflect the current Groq-only setup. Paid profile: GPT-4o-mini for planning/grading/checks; Sonnet 4.6 for synthesis.
Local collections stay inside this function until return. Empty-question return contains only relevant_chunks=[] and agent_synthesis=None.
Source: research_agent.py, retrieval.py, reranker.py, grader.py, prompts.py, llm_factory.py and builder.py. No API calls were made.
